send.title: Send
send.lede: Share a text, a file or an item from your vault through a link. It's encrypted in this browser, and its key travels after the # in the link, which never reaches the server.
send.none: No Sends yet. Make one on this page and its link shows up here.
send.name: Name
send.fileTooBig: That file is over {size}, the most a Send holds.
send.maxViewsInvalid: Type a whole number of 1 or more, or leave it empty.
send.hideEmail: Hide my email from whoever opens it
send.linkHint: The part after the last slash is the key. Anyone with the whole link can open the Send.
send.policy: A policy of one of your spaces forbids making this Send.
send.delete.title: Delete {name}?
send.delete.body: The link stops working at once and the Send cannot be brought back.
ie.title: Import & export
ie.lede: Files are read and written in this browser. An imported file never uploads; its items are encrypted here, then synced.
ie.drop: Drop a file here, or choose one
ie.passwordHint: Only for an encrypted export. Leave it empty for a plain file.
ie.passwordNeeded: This export is encrypted. Type the password it was made with.
ie.preview: {count, plural, one {# item is} other {# items are}} ready to import.
ie.warning.files: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} from the export can't be attached in this version and will be left out.
ie.warning.skipped: {count, plural, one {# entry was} other {# entries were}} left out: in the source's trash, or a kind Kemlock doesn't have.
ie.warning.spaces: The export names {count, plural, one {# shared vault} other {# shared vaults}}. Everything goes into the place you pick below.
ie.imported: {count, plural, one {Imported # item.} other {Imported # items.}} They sync to your apps now.
ie.export.kemlockHint: Opens with its password. Every kind of item.
ie.export.bitwardenHint: For moving to a Bitwarden or Vaultwarden account. Logins, cards, identities, notes, SSH keys.
ie.export.csvHint: Logins and notes only. Anyone who gets the file reads every password in it.
ie.csvWarning: A CSV file isn't encrypted. Keep it off shared folders and delete it after you use it.
ie.newPasswordHint: At least 8 characters. It isn't stored anywhere.
ie.error.tooLarge: That file is larger than Kemlock reads.
ie.error.limit: That export has more in it than Kemlock reads in one go.
ie.error.unsupported: That isn't an export Kemlock can read. Pick the app it came from in the list.
ie.error.malformed: The file is damaged or isn't shaped as that app writes it.
ie.error.passwordRequired: This export is encrypted. Type its password.
ie.error.badPassword: That password, or the key file, doesn't open the export.
ie.error.kdf: The export asks for more key-derivation work than Kemlock accepts.
ie.error.accountRestricted: This export is encrypted with an account key. Export it again with a password.
ie.error.encryption: This kind of encryption isn't supported.
ie.error.unavailable: The importer can't start in this build of the web vault.
dup.title: Duplicates
dup.lede: {count, plural, one {# group} other {# groups}} in your vault and spaces. Nothing merges until you pick what to keep, and merged items wait in the trash for 30 days.
dup.how.title: Found in this browser, from values that never left it
dup.how.body: This browser compared normalised values of the items it has opened, and checked that each group really matches. The server learned nothing.
dup.how.checked: Checked {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}.
dup.server.label: Let the server match new items
dup.server.hint: Not available: this server has no route for it. Matching stays in this browser.
dup.filter.label: Kind of duplicate
dup.none: No duplicates left. New ones show here as items are saved.
dup.why.account: Same website and username, different passwords
dup.preview.title: Merge preview
dup.preview.none: Pick a group to see what a merge keeps.
dup.preview.login: These logins can become one. Pick what the kept login holds.
dup.preview.other: These hold the same values. Keep one; the others go to the trash.
dup.preview.result: Keeps {name}. {trashed} goes to the trash for 30 days.
dup.pick.name: Name
dup.toast.merged: Merged into {kept}. {trashed} is in the trash for 30 days.
dup.toast.dismissed: {name} is marked as not duplicates in this browser.
merge.title: Merge {count} items into one
merge.lede: Pick what the kept item holds. Nothing is lost: the password you don't keep goes into its password history, and the other item waits in the trash for 30 days.
merge.how: Found and compared in this browser.
merge.newest: The most recently changed value is picked first.
merge.name: Name
merge.passkeyMoves: {name} passkey, moves to the kept login
merge.history: {count, plural, =0 {No password joins its history.} one {# other password joins its password history.} other {# other passwords join its password history.}}
merge.oneBatch: One batch: the kept item's new revision and the others' move to the trash are written together, or not at all.
merge.done: Merged into {kept}. {trashed} is in the trash for 30 days.
merge.done.title: Merged
merge.gone.title: These are no longer a group
merge.gone.body: One of them changed or was merged since you opened this page.
sites.title: Websites of {name}
sites.lede: {count, plural, one {One website} other {# websites}}. Each website has its own rule for where it's filled.
sites.defaultNote: Default fills a website on its base domain, as Kemlock always has.
sites.hint.empty: Type a website, such as example.co
sites.hint.default: Fills on {domain} and every site under it, as Kemlock does today
sites.hint.domain: Fills on {domain} and every site under it
sites.hint.exact: Browser: this address only. Phones: {host} only
sites.hint.startsWith: Browser: addresses that start with it. Phones: {host} only
sites.hint.regex: Browser extension only; phones never fill it
sites.hint.never: Kept as a record, never filled
sites.risky: Bitwarden calls this rule dangerous if used carelessly. Check what it matches.
sites.phonesNote: Phones see only the site's host, so path rules fill on their host. The browser extension checks the whole address.
sites.apps.bitwardenBody: The same list as the login's URIs, rules included, when it's kept in Bitwarden form
sites.apps.olderBody: The hosts, each filled on its base domain until the app updates
sites.apps.serverBody: Nothing: the list and its rules are inside the item's ciphertext
health.title: Vault health
health.lede: Worked out in this browser from the open vault. The server never learns which items have a problem.
health.fix: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing to fix} one {# thing to fix} other {# things to fix}}
health.exposed.detail: This password is in Pwned Passwords {count, number} times.
health.reused.detail: {count} logins share one password. A breach at one opens all of them.
health.noCode.detail: {count, plural, one {# service offers} other {# services offer}} two-step login and has no code in this vault: {sites}.
health.expiring.detail: The key expires on {date}, in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
health.expired.detail: The key expired on {date}, {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago.
health.good.synced: {count, plural, one {# item} other {All # items}} synced, end-to-end encrypted
health.hibp.label: Look passwords up in Pwned Passwords
health.hibp.hint: Sends the first 5 characters of each password's SHA-1 hash from this browser to Have I Been Pwned. The password and the rest of the hash stay here.
health.hibp.failed: Pwned Passwords couldn't be reached, so exposed passwords aren't shown. Check your connection and reload.
health.list.label: Keep the breach list up to date
health.list.hint: Not available: this server has no breach-list route yet, so breaches since you saved a login aren't checked.
failover.title: Where your vault is stored
failover.lede: Which servers hold each vault, and which one your apps are using now.
failover.banner: Your home server, {home}, is offline. Syncing through {replica}. Changes to members and keys wait until it's back.
failover.whereBody: Its home first, then its replicas in order. Your apps go back to the home once it has been up for 5 minutes.
failover.withheldBody: You chose not to send {name}'s copy the changes that were waiting. They are still on this server and on your other servers.
failover.apps.title: Your apps right now
failover.apps.body: Kemlock apps switch servers on their own. Bitwarden apps and Amethystora Vault stay on the home server's address and work from their local copy until it's back.
failover.single.title: One server
failover.single.body: This vault is stored on this server only. When federation is set up, its home and replicas are listed here.
sendAccess.title: Someone shared a Send with you
sendAccess.lede: It is decrypted in this browser with the key in the link. The server never gets the key.
sendAccess.badLink.title: This link is not a Send link
sendAccess.badLink.body: The link is cut short or changed. Ask the sender for the whole link, including the part after the last slash.
sendAccess.password.title: This Send has a password
sendAccess.password.lede: Type the password the sender gave you. It is turned into a proof in this browser; the server never sees the password.
sendAccess.password.label: Password
sendAccess.unavailable.title: This Send is not available
sendAccess.unavailable.body: It was deleted, it has expired, it has been opened as often as the sender allowed, or the link's key does not open it.
sendAccess.failed: The Send could not be opened. Check your connection and try again.
sendAccess.rateLimited: Too many tries. Wait {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} and try again.
sendAccess.rateLimitedNow: Too many tries. Wait a little and try again.
sendAccess.text.label: Text
sendAccess.file.failed: The file could not be downloaded or decrypted.
sendAccess.file.unavailable: The file is no longer available, or the key does not open it.
sendAccess.footer: Kemlock Send: the note or file is encrypted before it leaves the sender's browser.
sendItem.field.title: Title
sendItem.none: No items of this kind in your vault
sendItem.hint: Only the fields of the item go in the Send: no history, and nothing from other items.
sendItem.unreadable: This item could not be turned into a Send: it is too large or has nothing readable to send.
